categories.main_business_segments: Performance Food Group Company operates through three primary segments: Foodservice, Convenience, and Specialty. The Foodservice segment distributes a broad line of food and food-related products to independent and chain restaurants, as well as other institutional customers. The Convenience segment is a major wholesale distributor to convenience stores, drug stores, mass merchants, and small format retailers. The Specialty segment (formerly Vistar) focuses on distributing candy, snacks, beverages, and food items to vending, office coffee service, theaters, and retail channels.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: PFGC's core operations center on large-scale procurement, warehousing, and distribution, leveraging integrated computer systems for inventory management, route optimization, and order fulfillment. The company utilizes advanced logistics, custom-cut meat and seafood processing at select facilities, and increasingly incorporates technology such as AI and telematics to enhance supply chain efficiency, safety, and customer service. The company does not manufacture most products but adds value through custom processing, private label development, and operational consulting.
categories.primary_customers_markets: PFGC serves over 300,000 customer locations, including independent and chain restaurants, schools, healthcare facilities, business and industry sites, convenience stores, drug stores, mass merchants, theaters, vending distributors, and office coffee service providers. No single customer accounts for more than 10% of sales, reflecting a highly diversified customer base across the food-away-from-home and convenience retail industries.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates 155 distribution centers across the United States and Canada, with a particularly strong presence in North America. The Foodservice segment has expanded in the Southeastern U.S. through the Cheney Brothers acquisition. Distribution centers are strategically located to serve customers within 200-450 miles, ensuring broad national reach.
categories.supply_chain_position: PFGC operates as a downstream distributor, acting as an intermediary between food and consumer product manufacturers/suppliers and end customers such as restaurants, retailers, and institutional buyers. The company does not manufacture most products but adds value through distribution, logistics, and select processing services.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding sales to independent customers and proprietary Performance Brands, pursuing acquisitions (notably Cheney Brothers), enhancing procurement and supply chain efficiencies, and leveraging technology (including AI) for operational improvements. The company is also focused on sustainability, with goals to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and engage suppliers on climate targets, and invests in workforce development and safety.
categories.revenue_model: PFGC primarily generates revenue through the sale and distribution of food, beverages, tobacco, and related products. Revenue is recognized at the point of delivery, with pricing set by contract or at order, often as a markup over cost. The company also earns from value-added services, private label products, and promotional allowances from suppliers.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: The company competes in a highly fragmented and competitive industry, facing national, regional, and local distributors, including large players like Sysco and US Foods, as well as specialty and cooperative groups. PFGC is positioned as one of the largest foodservice and convenience distributors in North America, leveraging scale, geographic reach, and supply chain efficiency to compete.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For fiscal 2025, PFGC reported net sales of $63.3 billion, up 8.6% year-over-year, with Adjusted EBITDA of $1.77 billion. The company has demonstrated consistent growth through organic expansion and acquisitions, with significant increases in assets and revenue following the Cheney Brothers acquisition. Net income for 2025 was $340 million, reflecting margin pressures and increased interest and depreciation expenses.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: PFGC differentiates itself through its broad product assortment, proprietary Performance Brands, extensive distribution network, and value-added services such as menu development and operational consulting. The company emphasizes its ability to serve diverse customer needs with local market expertise, supply chain efficiency, and a focus on higher-margin independent customers and private label products.
